### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **62** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 81 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a645b2ddd65e8a9665b8c9da3be352fa20d74b23` — the merge of head `b90233124904660697c0cb92ee8e985f4e616fba` into base `50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a645b2ddd65e8a9665b8c9da3be352fa20d74b23 && git checkout a645b2ddd65e8a9665b8c9da3be352fa20d74b23
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20 b90233124904660697c0cb92ee8e985f4e616fba && git checkout -B drift-repro 50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20 && git merge --no-ff b90233124904660697c0cb92ee8e985f4e616fba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 50646f01f2a59dcddf548e8a1286479fd09a5e20` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b90233124904660697c0cb92ee8e985f4e616fba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.sealed-remedy-kind.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-override-declarations.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-override-gate.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/override-declaration.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-write-package-scope.ts, docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md (D2, D6, D9, D10, supersede table), .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/server.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/spec.md (all read at `origin/main` `3eb6dfcf9e`; the PR's files at the head)

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the spec on `main` and ADR-0146 as amended by #28486:

1. **Save door (`saveMetaItem`, so `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` and every authoring path) refuses six new shapes, `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`** — an undeclared same name inside the closure (overlay types answer the gate's own sentence; sealed types still answer the sealed sentence first), `overrides` on a non-pair package, a declaration naming a package outside the closure or one that ships no such item, `overrides` on an excluded type, on an `object`, and on `flow`/`action`. **Right.** Each is a refusal ADR-0146 D2/D6/D9/D10 and ruling A on #28390 declare; the rule reads `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION`, `isCustomizationPairOf` and `customizationPackageId` from `@objectstack/spec/kernel` and copies none of them; the type list is the spec's closed constant, as D2 requires. Outside the closure the verdict is `not_concerned`, so ADR-0048 §3.4's coexistence on a bare name stands (pinned: `control: outside the closure a same name coexists`). A package-less row is `not_concerned` (pinned), which is N-16's territory and is left alone, correctly.
2. **Save door admits the pair's declared override on an open type and stores it as the pair's own row** (`intent: runtime-only`, the sealed refusal skipped for it). **Right.** This is the capability the spec declared in N-08 (`overrides: { package, basedOn }` on the overridable schemas) and that no door delivered until now; `basedOn` is recorded and never judged, as D2 and "Decided here" item 2 require. The per-item `_lock` still runs after the gate, so a declared override of a locked base item stays `ITEM_LOCKED` — consistent with ADR-0010 §3.3 and with the PR's "codes and statuses stay" line.
3. **The sealed sentence on an open overridable type gains the declare-or-rename tail.** **Right in substance** (ADR-0146's supersede row for ADR-0126 §7.1 names exactly `refusePackagedBaseOverride` as the place the clone advice gives way); the tail is read from the classification, not transcribed (the `sealed-remedy-kind` pin). One wording gap is listed under ④ (should-fix 2).
4. **Promotion doors (`publishMetaItem`, `publishPackageDrafts`) judge the draft body under `promoteInto` and throw last before the store.** **Right.** A draft stored before the gate, or whose closure has since gained the name, is refused at promotion with the save door's judge and envelope, and the batch reports it in `failed` (pinned).
5. **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol` public surface widens by two values and five types** (`judgeOverrideWrite`, `overrideWriteItemsOf`, `OverrideWriteItem`, `OverrideWriteSubject`, `OverrideWriteClosure`, `OverrideWriteRule`, `OverrideWriteVerdict`), one export line. **Right**, and it is what makes the three doors one judgement rather than three twins; it is why `Clause-②: yes` carries the `(narrowing)` arm instead of `no`.
6. **`os validate` exits 1 on the same refusals, `errors[]` rows `{ path, code, rule, packageId, message }`, message equal to the judge's.** **Right.** The walk follows the closure through the artifact's own packages only; a base the artifact does not carry is invisible, which the module header says and the publish/install doors cover. A new `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` row records that `os build` does not run the gate. **Right per the parity test's own contract** (a validate-only gate is "a real gap in the build's direction, reported and not closed", and the row is the only honest place for it).
7. **`POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` refuses the delivered package `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` with `details.refusals` before any write; the `200` answer of a base (re)install gains an optional `overrideCollisions` key, omitted when empty.** **Right.** This is Wanted 3 and Wanted 4(a) at the door where a package's items actually enter as code (`manifest.register`), the retarget the seat's amendment granted and the epic's rider (`6553666595`) asked for. Collisions are listed, never refused — the dependent's item is the one to rename, which is D2's rule. A base read-only is `delivered || !isWritablePackage` (booted manifests and `system`/`cloud` scopes), the same predicate the lifecycle routes use.
8. **No `packages/spec/**` shape changes.** **Right for the shape, wrong for the ledger**: three new stamp sites of the registered code `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` in `@objectstack/cli` (`override-declarations.ts:48`, `:127`) and `@objectstack/cloud-connection` (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:2012`) have no owner-key row and no waiver in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, which is what the provenance guard is red on (③, ④ must-fix 1).
9. **`protocol.org-scoped-write-refused.test.ts` is not in the file list, so it is unchanged** — the card's standing requirement and ADR-0146's supersede row for ADR-0126 D4 wall 1. **Right.**
10. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`** gains three rows for the new test double's `findOne`/`update`/`delete` asserts, written by the gate's `--write`. Generated output, read not reviewed.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/28410-override-write-gate.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` all **minor**, with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none — REASON`, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body. **Consistent with what the diff publishes and with AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3**: a `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves (all three carry the gate), `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, and the arm is `yes` because the diff also widens (the metadata-protocol exports, the `overrideCollisions` key, the `rule`/`packageId` row fields). The migration the breaking changeset owes is the remedy an author applies — rename, or declare from `<base>.custom` — and the body states it; nothing authorable is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO mapping and no tombstone is owed. `Skills-docs: none` checks out: `git grep` of `skills/**` on `origin/main` finds no `overrides:` declaration and no `.custom` teaching. "Check Changeset" is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on `b9023312` (read 2026-11-01, two readings ~10 min apart):** `Lint · docs & code guards` is **failure** — `Error-code provenance guard` (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:error-code-provenance`): "3 stamp site(s) of a registered code with no provenance row", the three named in ①8 — and the required context `Lint & Repo Gates` has rolled up **failure** on it. The same job is **success** on the merge-base `35b178bd` and on `origin/main` `3eb6dfcf`, so this is the PR's own red, not a merge-base signature. `Test Core` shards 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 were still `in_progress` at the second reading; every other completed run is `success` or `skipped`. Judged on the code; the seat reads the shards before any landing step.
- **Lane red line (`lanes/server.md`: cards that change the metadata format or the acceptance face go to the spec seat, whether or not they touch `packages/spec`) — breached on the literal reading, escalated, not a code must-fix.** The PR declares `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` of itself: by AGENTS.md's own definition that is a change to what a metadata author can write, i.e. the acceptance face, and `lanes/spec.md` reads the contract face as "the same input's accept/reject result changed", which is exactly what this diff does at four doors. The card was cut by the epic under `domain:server` on the strength of the ADR naming the write gate in `metadata-protocol` and N-08 (spec seat) having landed the shape first, and the server lane's own file says such a card "goes back to triage" rather than being re-labelled by the seat. So: this review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the compensating control the rule asks for; the landing owes triage's acknowledgement (and the spec seat's pointer) that the gate's enforcement half is server work under N-08's closed constants — the record of that goes on the card, not in this PR. The must-fix below makes the ledger point moot in the other direction: the ledger append is the spec lane's pre-approved class (the code already exists under `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, the fallback is unchanged, pure append of the two packages' own sections), so no spec-seat signature is owed for it.
- **Open question (`os build` refusing too, recorded as `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES.findOverrideDeclarationRefusals`): safe to land open; it does not need deciding first.** The parity test's contract is that a validate-only gate is a reported gap, and this row is honest: an artifact a build emits with a refused declaration or an undeclared same name is refused at the managed install (gated here, before any write) and at the publish doors, so nothing is silently admitted — the cost is a late refusal, not a false acceptance. Answer to the dev's options: A, in a follow-up card, since it widens the card's named gate points and so needs the maintainer's word; the gate reads only the parsed stack, which the parity file names as the shape that belongs in both commands (`SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES`, like `checkDependencyRanges`, which is cross-package by construction for the same reason). The seat files that card and leaves the row where it is until then.
- **Dev flag: `installPackage` → marketplace managed install.** Answered by the seat's amendment (`6553315966`) and asked for by the epic's rider (`6553666595`); measured true in the cited code (`PackageInstallManifestSchema` takes no items; `importUnmanagedPackage` writes through the gated save door). The rider wanted "a test that installs such an artifact through POST on the install-local route and is refused": delivered as a handler-level test of the route (`rawApp.routes.get('POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local')`), which exercises the real handler and the real `evaluateOverrideWriteGate`; accepted.
- **Dev flag: tests beside their doors, not in `protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts`.** Correct — `metadata-protocol` cannot import `cli` or `cloud-connection`; the card's placement was unimplementable as written and the three suites pin the same judge's sentence by equality.
- **Dev flag: `rollbackMetaItem` computes the `override-artifact` intent from `isArtifactBacked` alone.** A rollback of the pair's declared override row would be judged as an artifact override by the repository. Carrier N-10/N-16, outside this card's doors; not blocking; the seat should file it rather than leave it as an acceptance note, since it is a reproducible contract gap once N-10's read serves the row.
- **Dev flag: file surface beyond the claim.** `override-declarations.ts` (+ test), `validate-override-declarations.test.ts`, `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` (the ledger row the parity test demands), `protocol.sealed-remedy-kind.test.ts` (the sealed one-sentence pin would otherwise go red), the engine-double JSON (`--write`). All within the lane and the amendment's intent; `protocol-package-install.ts` and `protocol-write-package-scope.ts` were named in the claim and not edited, which is right (the closure walk is read, not changed).
- **Limit worth recording, no fix owed:** `translation` is on D2's list but is deliberately not a `defineStack()` collection (`manifest-collection-spelling.test.ts` pins `translations` out of `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR`), so the `os validate` and install walks cannot see translation items by construction; the save door judges each translation write. Likewise a one-package `.custom` stack validated against a base the artifact does not carry: a declared item is judged with the base assumed to ship it, and an undeclared same name is invisible to validate; both are answered at the publish and install doors, and the module header says so.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; PR is draft, not armed; `needs:contract-review` is on. No `packages/spec/**`, `docs/adr/**` or other governed path in the file list.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away at the consumer.** On `main` before this head, N-08's schemas accept `overrides: { package, basedOn }` on every overridable type and ADR-0146 D2 says the declaration is admitted from the pair alone and refused everywhere else, yet no door read it: a partner's same-named view published `200` (#28238) and a customer's `.custom` had no way to declare a replacement. That is a declared capability not delivered — an implementation gap — and the diff closes it on the producer side (ADR-0146's own words for the gate), in one pure rule read from the spec's constants, asked at the save door, the promotion, `os validate` and the managed install. The admit is real (the pair's row is stored with its declaration and promoted as runtime-only; N-10's read on `main` serves it), and every refusal is one the ADR names, with the ADR's sentence. Nothing a consumer could do before and the spec sanctions is removed: package-less overlay rows (N-16's), items outside the closure, and the hatch are untouched, and the precondition count (0 same-named closure rows in hotcrm `a598256` and the examples) says no existing deployment content is refused by it. Read against the acceptance scenarios on the card (Wanted 1–4, 6) each holds in the tree, not only in the PR body.

Tried to break it:

- *Closure and shippers.* The protocol reads the closure through `resolveWritePackageScope` (transitive, `resolvePackageClosure`) and shippers through `shippedArtifactsOf`, filtered to read-only packages inside the closure. A registry that cannot produce the written package answers `not_concerned`, and `uninstalledNamedBaseRefusal` already refuses that write — the fail-closed direction is kept. A writable shipper is not a base (ADR-0070: edited in place), which is right and keeps no booted or marketplace package out.
- *Ordering at the save door.* A refused declaration throws early (so a declared `flow` reads D9's sentence, not Regime C's clone sentence); the undeclared same name throws last, so a view container's 400 and a lock's `ITEM_LOCKED` keep their codes — verified in the head's `protocol.ts` (gate at the strip, sealed check skipped only for `admit`, the last throw just before the intent is chosen).
- *Install door.* Judged on the converted body before step 3's `register`; multi-package artifacts judged per entry under their own ids; a delivered package's items are read off the body so the gate never asks the registry about a package not yet in it; a reinstall of a dependent does not count its own old version as a dependent (`installedIds` excludes delivered ids). The collision scan reads dependents through `getMetaItems({ type, packageId })`, which is the protocol's listing, so a `.custom` built in Studio is covered as the dev says.
- *Second declarer.* After the pair declares, a partner declaring the same item is refused (pinned), which is ruling A's whole point.

Findings:

1. **Must-fix — the head is red on its own change: three `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` stamp sites with no provenance row.** `packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts:48` and `:127` (the `--json` `errors[].code` the command prints) and `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:2012` (the plugin's own Hono route answering 403) are real emitters of a registered code, and `check:error-code-provenance` fails the `Lint · docs & code guards` job and, through it, the required `Lint & Repo Gates`. The fix the gate itself prints: a row under `'@objectstack/cli'` and under `'@objectstack/cloud-connection'` in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, each with a comment naming the wire path (for cli, `door: 'none'` — a CLI exit, like the `STACK_PROVENANCE_MISSING` row beside it; for cloud-connection, the install-local route, like its `INSTALL_MODE_NOT_PERMITTED` row). Not a waiver: these doors name the vocabulary themselves and the row is the shape the ledger already uses for `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`'s other three emitters. The rows are the spec lane's pre-approved append class (`lanes/spec.md`: the code's existence was ruled on its owning card, the fallback is unchanged, pure append of the stamping package's own section), so the PR may carry them; the PR body's "No `packages/spec/**` file changes" line and the changeset's "the diff touches no `packages/spec/**` file" sentence in the ADR-0087 marker must then be rewritten to say what the diff does touch (the marker's disposition stays `not-required`: a ledger row is not a type-surface or runtime-interface change). The new head is a substantive head and owes a fresh full review.
2. **Should-fix — the sealed tail names a route a non-pair writer does not have.** `sealedDeclareOrRenameTail` is appended for every writer of a sealed overridable type (`page`, `app`, `dataset`, `doc`, `book`, `mapping`), and because the sealed refusal runs before the gate's undeclared-same-name throw, a partner package's undeclared same-named `page` reads "declare an override from '<base>.custom' …, or rename the item", whereas ADR-0146 D2 says a non-pair dependent is told the one fix it has, rename; the gate's own partner sentence (pinned for `view`/`dashboard`) is reached only on overlay types. Code and status are right, both fixes named are real routes in the deployment, and the item's author can act on "rename", so this is wording, not acceptance; the cheap cure is to pass the request's `packageId` into the tail and print the pair clause only when the writer is the pair (or no package), keeping the one-sentence pin.
3. **Should-fix — a malformed `overrides` is answered by the gate, not the schema.** The gate runs at the decoration strip, ~800 lines ahead of the per-type Zod gate, and `declarationOf` treats any present `overrides` (including `null`, a non-object, or one without `package`) as a declaration, so a body the schema would refuse `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (`OverrideDeclarationSchema` requires `package` and `basedOn`) is answered `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE declared_outside_pair` with the pair sentence. The sentence does say "naming the base in `overrides.package`", so the author is not misled, and `os validate` runs the schema first, but the save door's code is the gate's where the fact is the schema's. Either let a declaration that is not an object with a string `package` fall through to the schema gate, or move the declared-case throw after it; one test either way.
